assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why center the sample in the field of view before focusing?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use diagrams and illustrations to describe the arrangement, spacing, and relative motion of the particles in each of the three states (phases) of matter
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains microscope specimen centering, which is unrelated to the particle model of matter or the arrangement/spacing/motion of particles in states of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why center the sample in the field of view before focusing?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses microscope technique, not particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects on particles.

copy.en:
Why center the sample in the field of view before focusing?

Because when you switch to a higher power objective, the microscope zooms in on the center of the field of view!
copy.tl:
Bakit dapat isentro ang sample sa field of view bago mag-focus?

Dahil kapag lumipat ka sa mas mataas na power na objective, ang microscope ay mag-zoom in sa gitna ng field of view!
copy.bis:
Ngano isentro ang sample sa field of view sa dili pa mag-focus?

Tungod kay kung mobalhin ka sa mas taas nga power nga objective, ang microscope mag-zoom in sa tunga sa field of view!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: At 0°C, sound travels through air at 331 meters per second
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the speed of sound in air and its temperature dependence, which is a physics topic. G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system and major celestial objects. There is no overlap in subject matter.

copy.en: At 0°C, sound travels through air at 331 meters per second, and for every 1°C increase in temperature, its speed increases by 0.6 m/s.
copy.tl: Sa 0°C, ang tunog ay naglalakbay sa hangin sa bilis na 331 metro bawat segundo, at sa bawat 1°C na pagtaas ng temperatura, ang bilis nito ay tumataas ng 0.6 m/s.
copy.bis: Sa 0°C, ang tingog mobiyahe sa hangin sa kakusgon nga 331 metros matag segundo, ug sa matag 1°C nga pagtaas sa temperatura, ang kakusgon niini motaas og 0.6 m/s.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Acceleration is a change in speed over time
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the physics concept of acceleration (change in speed over time). G3-L-4 requires observing and describing animal outer body parts and their roles in movement and food gathering. There is no connection to animal anatomy or living things; the card is entirely unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Acceleration is a change in speed over time, so a car that goes from 0 to 60 kilometers per hour in 5 seconds is accelerating.
copy.tl: Ang acceleration ay pagbabago ng bilis sa paglipas ng panahon, kaya ang isang kotse na mula 0 hanggang 60 kilometro bawat oras sa loob ng 5 segundo ay nag-a-accelerate.
copy.bis: Ang acceleration mao ang pagbag-o sa kadasigon sa paglabay sa panahon, busa ang usa ka kotse nga gikan sa 0 ngadto sa 60 ka kilometro matag oras sa 5 ka segundo nag-a-accelerate.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Spermatogenesis is the process in the testes, the male reproductive organs, where one diploid cell divides by meiosis to produce four haploid sperm cells.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes spermatogenesis, a biological process of sperm production. G9-L-10 concerns effects of human activities (deforestation, pollution, invasive species) on ecosystems. No connection.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Spermatogenesis is the process in the testes, the male reproductive organs, where one diploid cell divides by meiosis to produce four haploid sperm cells.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a cellular reproductive process, not interactions between living things or between living and non-living things. G6-L-8 is about ecological interactions bringing good or harm; spermatogenesis is unrelated.

copy.en: Spermatogenesis is the process in the testes, the male reproductive organs, where one diploid cell divides by meiosis to produce four haploid sperm cells.
copy.tl: Ang spermatogenesis ay ang proseso sa testes, ang male reproductive organs, kung saan ang isang diploid cell ay nahahati sa pamamagitan ng meiosis para makabuo ng apat na haploid sperm cells.
copy.bis: Ang spermatogenesis mao ang proseso sa testes, ang male reproductive organs, diin ang usa ka diploid cell mabahin pinaagi sa meiosis aron makahimo ug upat ka haploid sperm cells.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Both spiders and silkworms make silk, but a spider uses its silk as a safety dragline, while a silkworm spins its silk into a cocoon.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses silk production and use, not life-cycle stages, and does not use a flow chart or compare developmental stages.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Both spiders and silkworms make silk, but a spider uses its silk as a safety dragline, while a silkworm spins its silk into a cocoon.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe outer body parts of animals or their roles in movement and food gathering.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Both spiders and silkworms make silk, but a spider uses its silk as a safety dragline, while a silkworm spins its silk into a cocoon.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe how animals have changed to suit their environment; it only contrasts silk use.

copy.en: Both spiders and silkworms make silk, but a spider uses its silk as a safety dragline, while a silkworm spins its silk into a cocoon.
copy.tl: Parehong gumagawa ng sutla ang gagamba at ang uod ng silkworm, pero ginagamit ng gagamba ang sutla bilang dragline para sa kaligtasan, habang ang silkworm ay gumagawa ng cocoon.
copy.bis: Parehong mohimo og seda ang lawalawa ug ang ulod sa silkworm, apan gigamit sa lawalawa ang seda ingong dragline alang sa kaluwasan, samtang ang silkworm mohimo og cocoon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Echinoderms are marine animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe some of the materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes echinoderms (marine animals with spiny endoskeletons, water vascular system, tube feet), which is unrelated to identifying and describing materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines. The competency is about volcanic materials such as lava, ash, and tephra.

copy.en: Echinoderms are marine animals like sea stars and sea urchins that have spiny endoskeletons, a water vascular system, and tube feet.
copy.tl: Ang mga echinoderm ay mga marine animal tulad ng sea star at sea urchin na may spiny endoskeleton, water vascular system, at tube feet.
copy.bis: Ang mga echinoderm mga marine animal sama sa sea star ug sea urchin nga adunay spiny endoskeleton, water vascular system, ug tube feet.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Passing an electrical current through some compounds can break the chemical bonds and separate them back into their elements.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use diagrams and illustrations to describe the arrangement, spacing, and relative motion of the particles in each of the three states (phases) of matter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses electrolysis breaking chemical bonds, not the arrangement, spacing, or motion of particles in the three states of matter. No diagrams or illustrations of states are involved.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Passing an electrical current through some compounds can break the chemical bonds and separate them back into their elements.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects. It is about chemical decomposition by electricity, not the particle model of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Passing an electrical current through some compounds can break the chemical bonds and separate them back into their elements.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the Particle Model of Matter as 'All matter is made up of tiny particles with each pure substance having its own kind of particles.'
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe the Particle Model of Matter (all matter made of tiny particles with each pure substance having its own kind). It addresses breaking compounds into elements, which is a chemical change concept.

copy.en:
Can a compound be broken apart?

Yes! Passing an electrical current through some compounds can break the chemical bonds and separate them back into their elements.
copy.tl:
Maaari bang paghiwalayin ang isang compound?

Oo! Ang pagdaan ng electrical current sa ilang compound ay kayang putulin ang chemical bonds at paghiwalayin sila pabalik sa kanilang mga element.
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang bulagon ang usa ka compound?

Oo! Ang pag-agi sa electrical current sa pipila ka compound makaputol sa chemical bonds ug magbulag kanila balik sa ilang mga element.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: molds and bacteria
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses spoiled chocolate candies and the health risk from molds and bacteria. It has no connection to making an electromagnet or observing its properties.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: molds and bacteria
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about food spoilage and microorganisms, not about magnets or investigating their properties. It does not support the competency in any way.

copy.en: If chocolate candies have spoiled, throw them away so the molds and bacteria on them cannot make anyone sick.
copy.tl: Kapag ang mga chocolate candy ay nasira na, itapon na ito para hindi makapagdulot ng sakit ang mga molds at bacteria na nasa mga ito.
copy.bis: Kon ang mga chocolate candy nadaot na, ilabay kini aron ang mga molds ug bacteria nga anaa niini dili makapasakit ni bisan kinsa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a spore case opens, the tiny spores are released
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes spore release and development, which is unrelated to the digestive system parts (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) or their functions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a spore case opens, the tiny spores are released
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about spore dispersal and germination, not about human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory).

copy.en: When a spore case opens, the tiny spores are released and may be carried by wind or water, and once a spore lands in a favorable environment, it develops into a new organism.
copy.tl: Kapag bumukas ang spore case, ang maliliit na spores ay inilalabas at maaaring dalhin ng hangin o tubig, at kapag dumapo ang spore sa magandang kapaligiran, ito ay nagiging bagong organismo.
copy.bis: Kon moabli ang spore case, ang gagmay nga mga spores ipagawas ug mahimong dalhon sa hangin o tubig, ug kon ang spore motugpa sa maayong palibot, kini mahimong bag-ong organismo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: place the glass slide on the flat stage and secure it with the stage clips
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes using the microscope stage and clips to hold a slide, which is unrelated to reflection/refraction of light using mirrors, lenses, or prisms.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: place the glass slide on the flat stage and secure it with the stage clips
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about microscope slide handling, not comparing wavelengths and frequencies of electromagnetic waves.

copy.en: To observe a specimen, place the glass slide on the flat stage and secure it with the stage clips so it does not move.
copy.tl: Para tingnan ang specimen, ilagay ang glass slide sa patag na stage at i-secure ito gamit ang stage clips para hindi ito gumalaw.
copy.bis: Aron tan-awon ang specimen, ibutang ang glass slide sa patag nga stage ug i-secure kini gamit ang stage clips aron dili kini molihok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists use standardized tools and metric units like centimeters and milliliters
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about standardized measurement and metric units, not about sources of light, how light behaves, or its uses. It does not support the G3-F-6 competency.

copy.en:
What if everyone used different-sized spoons to measure medicine?

It would be dangerous because the amounts would not be the same. Scientists use standardized tools and metric units like centimeters and milliliters so measurements are accurate and consistent everywhere.
copy.tl:
Paano kung iba-ibang laki ng kutsara ang gamitin ng lahat para sumukat ng gamot?

Delikado iyon dahil hindi magkakapareho ang dami. Gumagamit ang mga scientist ng standardized na mga tool at metric units tulad ng centimeters at milliliters para maging tumpak at pare-pareho ang sukat kahit saan.
copy.bis:
Unsa kaha kung lain-laing gidak-on sa kutsara ang gamiton sa tanan aron mosukod ug tambal?

Delikado kana tungod kay dili managsama ang gidaghanon. Ang mga scientist mogamit ug standardized nga mga tool ug metric units sama sa centimeters ug milliliters aron mahimong tukma ug parehas ang sukod bisan asa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A hot blue star burns its fuel super fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses star color and lifespan, which is stellar evolution, not the structure of the solar system, names of major celestial objects, their features, or composition. It does not support the competency.

copy.en: A hot blue star burns its fuel super fast, giving it a much shorter life than a cool red star. So, a star's color hints at how long it will live!
copy.tl: Ang mainit na asul na bituin mabilis gumamit ng gatong, kaya mas maikli ang buhay nito kaysa sa malamig na pulang bituin. Ang kulay ay nagpapahiwatig kung gaano katagal mabubuhay ito!
copy.bis: Ang init nga asul nga bituon paspas kaayo mogamit sa gatong, mao nga mas mubo ang kinabuhi niini kompara sa bugnaw nga pula. Ang kolor nagtimailhan kung unsa kadugay mabuhi kini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It looks for the start codon AUG!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about protein translation and the start codon AUG, which is molecular biology. The competency concerns observing and recording weather changes, which is entirely unrelated.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It looks for the start codon AUG!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the start codon AUG and methionine in protein translation, not weather characteristics such as temperature, pressure, wind, or humidity. No instructional support for this weather competency.

copy.en:
How does the ribosome know where to start making a protein?

It looks for the start codon AUG! This special three-base code tells the ribosome to begin translation and also codes for the amino acid methionine.
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ng ribosome kung saan magsisimulang gumawa ng protina?

Hinahanap nito ang start codon na AUG! Ang espesyal na three-base code na ito ang nagsasabi sa ribosome na simulan ang translation at nagko-code din ito para sa amino acid na methionine.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagkahibalo sa ribosome kon asa magsugod paghimo ug protina?

Gipangita niya ang start codon nga AUG! Kining espesyal nga three-base code nagsulti sa ribosome nga sugdan ang translation ug nag-code usab kini para sa amino acid nga methionine.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: activation energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains activation energy for chemical reactions, which is unrelated to plate boundaries, structures, movements, or events at plate boundaries.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: activation energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses activation energy in chemistry, not earthquake effects on communities or magnitude, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en:
Why do some reactions need a spark to start?

Particles need a minimum amount of energy, called activation energy, to begin reacting. A spark gives them that starting push!
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng spark para magsimula ang ilang reactions?

Kailangan ng mga particle ng minimum na energy, na tinatawag na activation energy, upang magsimulang mag-react. Ang spark ang nagbibigay ng panimulang tulak na iyon!
copy.bis:
Ngano ang uban nga reactions nagkinahanglan ug spark aron magsugod?

Ang mga particle nagkinahanglan ug minimum nga energy, nga gitawag ug activation energy, aron magsugod sa pag-react. Ang spark maoy mohatag nianang pagsugod nga pagtulod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Solutions are not always liquids
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the physical states of solutions (solid, liquid, gas) and the states of solute and solvent. This is chemistry content about solutions, not the human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) required by G4-L-1. The assigned code is unrelated to the card's subject.

copy.en: Solutions are not always liquids; they may be solids, liquids, or gases, and the solute and solvent can be in any of these states.
copy.tl: Ang solution ay hindi laging liquid; maaari itong solid, liquid, o gas, at ang solute at solvent ay maaaring nasa alinman sa mga anyong ito.
copy.bis: Ang solution dili kanunay liquid; mahimo kini nga solid, liquid, o gas, ug ang solute ug solvent mahimong naa sa bisan asa niining mga kahimtang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a 'spark plug' makes a tiny spark to light the fuel and make the engine run.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the ignition spark in an engine, not static electricity or investigations with common materials such as a comb, plastic/glass rods, or balloons. It does not support the competency.

copy.en: Not all sparks are just surprising—some are useful! In a car or motorcycle engine, a 'spark plug' makes a tiny spark to light the fuel and make the engine run.
copy.tl: Hindi lahat ng spark ay nakakagulat! Sa makina ng kotse o motor, ang 'spark plug' ay gumagawa ng maliit na spark para sindihan ang gasolina at patakbuhin ang makina.
copy.bis: Dili tanan nga spark makakurat ra! Sa makina sa sakyanan o motor, ang 'spark plug' mohimo ug gamay nga spark aron dagkutan ang gasolina ug padaganon ang makina.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A stationary object does not move
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a stationary object (a book at rest), which is about motion/rest, not about heat energy or changes of state. It provides no instructional support for the role of heat energy in melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A stationary object does not move
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about an object not moving, unrelated to changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes (solid→liquid→vapor, vapor→liquid→solid). No support for this competency.

copy.en: A stationary object does not move, like a book resting quietly on a table.
copy.tl: Ang stationary object ay hindi gumagalaw, tulad ng isang librong nakapatong nang tahimik sa mesa.
copy.bis: Ang stationary object dili molihok, sama sa usa ka libro nga nagpahulay nga hilom sa lamesa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A larger launch angle sends the projectile higher
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes projectile motion (launch angle and maximum height), a physics topic. G10-M-4 concerns chemical reactions and their environmental impact; there is no chemistry content or support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A larger launch angle sends the projectile higher
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe important types of chemical reactions (combination, decomposition, single replacement, double replacement)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about projectile launch angle and height, not about types of chemical reactions (combination, decomposition, single replacement, double replacement). The assigned chemistry competency is unrelated to the card's physics content.

copy.en: A larger launch angle sends the projectile higher, so the maximum height increases as the angle of release becomes steeper.
copy.tl: Ang mas malaking launch angle ay nagpapataas ng projectile, kaya tumataas ang maximum height habang nagiging mas matarik ang anggulo ng paglunsad.
copy.bis: Ang mas dako nga launch angle nagpataas sa projectile, mao nga motaas ang maximum height samtang nagkatarik ang anggulo sa paglunsad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can record the Sun's apparent movement safely by marking the shadow of a stick on the ground at different times
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: A stick-shadow Sun record is unrelated to identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels.

copy.en: You can record the Sun's apparent movement safely by marking the shadow of a stick on the ground at different times, without looking directly at the Sun.
copy.tl: Maaari mong i-record ang paggalaw ng Araw nang ligtas sa pamamagitan ng pagmarka sa anino ng isang stick sa lupa sa iba't ibang oras, nang hindi direktang tumitingin sa Araw.
copy.bis: Mahimo nimong i-record ang paglihok sa Adlaw nga luwas pinaagi sa pagmarka sa anino sa usa ka stick sa yuta sa lain-laing oras, nga dili direktang motan-aw sa Adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a cool, dry place away from heat, like a cabinet far from the stove or sink, and out of children's reach!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about safe storage of medicines at home, which has no relation to making or observing an electromagnet. It does not support any part of the competency.

copy.en:
Where should medicines be stored at home?

In a cool, dry place away from heat, like a cabinet far from the stove or sink, and out of children's reach!
copy.tl:
Saan dapat itago ang mga gamot sa bahay?

Sa malamig at tuyong lugar na malayo sa init, tulad ng cabinet na malayo sa kalan o lababo, at hindi maaabot ng mga bata!
copy.bis:
Asa man dapat tipigan ang mga tambal sa balay?

Sa bugnaw ug uga nga lugar nga layo sa init, sama sa cabinet nga layo sa stove o lababo, ug dili maabot sa mga bata!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Neptune has dark-colored storms in its atmosphere
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using flow charts and labeled diagrams explain the role of plants and animals in the cycles of nature, such as the carbon, oxygen, and water cycles
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about Neptune's storms and its distance from the Sun. It provides no information about plants, animals, or the carbon, oxygen, or water cycles, and does not use flow charts or labeled diagrams.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Neptune has dark-colored storms in its atmosphere
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card contains nothing about photosynthesis or respiration, their raw materials, or products. It is an astronomy fact about Neptune.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Neptune has dark-colored storms in its atmosphere
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, or shelter. It is unrelated to living things entirely.

copy.en: Neptune has dark-colored storms in its atmosphere and is sometimes farther from the Sun than Pluto is.
copy.tl: Ang Neptune ay may madidilim na bagyo sa atmosphere nito at minsan ay mas malayo sa Sun kaysa sa Pluto.
copy.bis: Ang Neptune adunay mangitngit nga mga bagyo sa iyang atmosphere ug usahay mas layo sa Sun kaysa sa Pluto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Constellations like Pegasus, Taurus, Aquarius, Libra, Leo, and Gemini are named after figures from ancient stories
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses constellations and their mythological names, which is unrelated to observing the root and shoot system in plants or describing their importance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Constellations like Pegasus, Taurus, Aquarius, Libra, Leo, and Gemini are named after figures from ancient stories
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about constellations and ancient stories, not about how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet basic needs.

copy.en: Constellations like Pegasus, Taurus, Aquarius, Libra, Leo, and Gemini are named after figures from ancient stories, each with a recognizable star pattern.
copy.tl: Ang mga constellation tulad ng Pegasus, Taurus, Aquarius, Libra, Leo, at Gemini ay pinangalanan mula sa mga tauhan ng sinaunang kuwento, bawat isa ay may nakikilalang pattern ng bituin.
copy.bis: Ang mga constellation sama sa Pegasus, Taurus, Aquarius, Libra, Leo, ug Gemini ginganlan gikan sa mga karakter sa karaang sugilanon, matag usa adunay mailhan nga pattern sa bituon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A stretched rubber band stores elastic potential energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes elastic potential energy in a stretched rubber band, which is a physics concept about energy storage. G6-M-1 requires describing changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) using diagrams and flowcharts. The card provides no information about phase changes or state transitions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A stretched rubber band stores elastic potential energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: G5-M-6 requires describing how temperature changes cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). The card is about elastic potential energy, not about temperature-induced phase changes. There is no connection to matter states or temperature.

copy.en: A stretched rubber band stores elastic potential energy, which is energy kept inside objects that can act like springs and snap back into shape.
copy.tl: Ang nabanat na rubber band ay nagtatago ng elastic potential energy, ang energy na nakaimbak sa mga bagay na kayang kumilos tulad ng spring at bumalik sa dating hugis.
copy.bis: Ang nabinat nga rubber band nagtago ug elastic potential energy, ang energy nga gitipigan sa mga butang nga makalihok sama sa spring ug mobalik sa orihinal nga porma.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: strike-slip fault

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about fault mechanics, not about ecosystem population growth slowing near carrying capacity.

copy.en: In a strike-slip fault, the fault plane is nearly vertical and the rocks slide past each other horizontally.
copy.tl: Sa strike-slip fault, ang fault plane ay halos patayo at ang mga bato ay dumudulas nang pahalang sa isa't isa.
copy.bis: Sa strike-slip fault, ang fault plane hapit patindog ug ang mga bato modahili nga pinahigda sa usag usa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Well-constructed houses made of reinforced concrete can survive Signal 3 with only minor roof damage, but may suffer major damage at Signal 5.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about house construction and storm signal impacts, not about using observing, predicting, or measuring skills in guided science activities. No process skills are taught or demonstrated.

copy.en: Well-constructed houses made of reinforced concrete can survive Signal 3 with only minor roof damage, but may suffer major damage at Signal 5.
copy.tl: Ang mga matibay na bahay na gawa sa reinforced concrete ay kayang makaligtas sa Signal 3 na may minor lang na pinsala sa bubong, ngunit maaaring magkaroon ng malaking pinsala sa Signal 5.
copy.bis: Ang mga lig-on nga balay nga hinimo sa reinforced concrete makalahutay sa Signal 3 nga adunay minor lang nga kadaot sa atop, apan mahimong makakuha ug dako nga kadaot sa Signal 5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its electron structure, especially the number of valence electrons, determines its group and period!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify inertia as the tendency for an object to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how an element's electron structure (valence electrons) determines its position on the periodic table. This is a chemistry concept, not the physics concept of inertia (tendency to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force). The card provides no information about inertia.

copy.en:
Why is an element located where it is on the periodic table?

Its electron structure, especially the number of valence electrons, determines its group and period!
copy.tl:
Bakit matatagpuan ang isang elemento sa kinaroroonan nito sa periodic table?

Ang electron structure nito, lalo na ang bilang ng valence electron, ang tumutukoy sa grupo at period nito!
copy.bis:
Ngano ang usa ka elemento nahimutang sa nahimutangan sa periodic table?

Ang electron structure, ilabi na ang gidaghanon sa valence electron, maoy motino sa grupo ug period!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Subduction is when old, dense oceanic crust sinks into the mantle and melts, recycling the seafloor back into Earth's interior.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses

The card provides no information about the Sun, Moon, Earth motions, seasons, or eclipses, so it does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Subduction is when old, dense oceanic crust sinks into the mantle and melts, recycling the seafloor back into Earth's interior.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: G3-E-7 is about observing and recording how the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars move across the sky. The card is about plate tectonics and subduction, with no connection to celestial objects or their apparent motion. It is unrelated to this competency.

copy.en: Subduction is when old, dense oceanic crust sinks into the mantle and melts, recycling the seafloor back into Earth's interior.
copy.tl: Ang subduction ay ang paglubog ng luma at mabigat na oceanic crust sa mantle at pagkatunaw nito, na nire-recycle ang seafloor pabalik sa loob ng Earth.
copy.bis: Ang subduction mao ang pag-unlod sa daan ug dasok nga oceanic crust sa mantle ug pagkatunaw, nga gi-recycle ang seafloor balik sa sulod sa Earth.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses covalent bonding in sugar, a chemistry topic. G10-F-8 is about conservation of momentum in collisions, which is unrelated to the card's content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Table sugar, with the formula C12H22O11, is a covalent compound
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that momentum depends on the mass and the velocity of a moving object that can be used to predict the impact the object will have if it hits another object
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why sugar is a covalent compound. G10-F-4 concerns momentum depending on mass and velocity, a physics concept with no connection to the card's chemistry content.

copy.en: Table sugar, with the formula C12H22O11, is a covalent compound because carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen are all nonmetals.
copy.tl: Ang table sugar, na may formula na C12H22O11, ay isang covalent compound dahil ang carbon, hydrogen, at oxygen ay pawang mga nonmetals.
copy.bis: Ang table sugar, nga adunay formula nga C12H22O11, usa ka covalent compound tungod kay ang carbon, hydrogen, ug oxygen pulos mga nonmetals.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Carbohydrates include sugars, which taste sweet, and starches, which are long chains of sugar units stored in foods like rice and bread.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the chemical composition of carbohydrates (sugars and starches). It does not address the properties of solids, liquids, or gases in terms of shape and volume, which is the focus of G5-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Carbohydrates include sugars, which taste sweet, and starches, which are long chains of sugar units stored in foods like rice and bread.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses carbohydrates as a nutrient, not the physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. No direct or prerequisite support for G3-M-5.

copy.en: Carbohydrates include sugars, which taste sweet, and starches, which are long chains of sugar units stored in foods like rice and bread.
copy.tl: Kasama sa carbohydrates ang sugars na matamis, at ang starches na mahahabang kadena ng sugar units na nakaimbak sa mga pagkain tulad ng kanin at tinapay.
copy.bis: Ang carbohydrates naglakip sa sugars nga tam-is, ug sa starches nga tag-as nga kadena sa sugar units nga gitipigan sa mga pagkaon sama sa kan-on ug pan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sulfur helps give proteins their shape
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses sulfur's role in protein structure and function, which is biochemistry. It does not address particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects as required by G7-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sulfur helps give proteins their shape
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sulfur in proteins, not about the three states of matter (solids, liquids, gases). It provides no instructional support for G5-M-2.

copy.en: Sulfur helps give proteins their shape, and the bonds it forms are important for proteins to perform their functions in the body.
copy.tl: Ang sulfur ay tumutulong sa pagbibigay ng hugis sa mga protina, at ang mga bond na nabubuo nito ay mahalaga para magampanan ng mga protina ang kanilang mga tungkulin sa katawan.
copy.bis: Ang sulfur makatabang sa paghatag ug porma sa mga protina, ug ang mga bond nga maporma kini importante aron mahimo sa mga protina ang ilang mga buluhaton sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: temperatures in the frigid zones stay below 10°C
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses polar summer temperatures, not the role of heat energy in change of state processes. No connection to melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: temperatures in the frigid zones stay below 10°C
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe changes of state for solids, liquids, or gases, nor does it use diagrams or flowcharts. It only states a temperature fact about polar regions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: temperatures in the frigid zones stay below 10°C
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about polar climate temperature, not the water cycle or its role in the environment. No mention of evaporation, condensation, precipitation, or water movement.

copy.en:
Does summer ever feel warm in the polar regions?

No! Even during summer months, temperatures in the frigid zones stay below 10°C, so it never feels like summer at all!
copy.tl:
Umiinit ba ang pakiramdam ng summer sa polar regions?

Hindi! Kahit sa mga buwan ng summer, ang temperatura sa frigid zones ay nananatiling mababa sa 10°C, kaya hindi talaga ito parang summer!
copy.bis:
Moinit ba ang pamati sa summer sa polar regions?

Dili! Bisan sa mga bulan sa summer, ang temperatura sa frigid zones magpabilin nga ubos sa 10°C, busa dili gyud kini sama sa summer!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun is not at the center of a planet's elliptical orbit

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses orbital mechanics and the Sun's position in a planet's elliptical orbit. G8-M-4 is about properties of pure substances, elements, compounds, and atomic protons. There is no connection to matter or chemistry.

copy.en: The Sun is not at the center of a planet's elliptical orbit; it sits at one of the two foci, which is why the planet is sometimes closer to the Sun.
copy.tl: Ang Araw ay wala sa gitna ng elliptical orbit ng isang planeta; ito ay nasa isa sa dalawang foci, kaya minsan ang planeta ay mas malapit sa Araw.
copy.bis: Ang Adlaw wala sa tunga sa elliptical orbit sa usa ka planeta; kini anaa sa usa sa duha ka foci, mao nga usahay ang planeta mas duol sa Adlaw.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about solar altitude and seasonal energy, not covalent bonding in water or carbon dioxide. G9-M-7 requires explaining covalent bond formation, which is entirely absent from the card.

copy.en: The height of the Sun in the sky changes with the seasons, and a higher Sun means more direct rays and more energy received by the ground.
copy.tl: Nagbabago ang taas ng araw sa langit kasabay ng mga panahon, at ang mas mataas na araw ay nangangahulugan ng mas direct na sinag at mas maraming energy na natatanggap ng lupa.
copy.bis: Ang gitas-on sa adlaw sa langit mausab uban sa mga panahon, ug ang mas taas nga adlaw nagpasabot ug mas direct nga silaw ug mas daghang energy nga madawat sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun takes a longer, higher path across the sky in summer and a shorter, lower path in winter, changing how long daylight lasts.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: G3-E-2 is about identifying useful things made from non-living materials and the natural materials used. The card discusses the Sun's seasonal path and daylight length, which is unrelated to this competency.

copy.en: The Sun takes a longer, higher path across the sky in summer and a shorter, lower path in winter, changing how long daylight lasts.
copy.tl: Mas mahaba at mas mataas ang daanan ng Araw sa langit tuwing summer at mas maikli at mas mababa tuwing winter, na nagbabago sa haba ng liwanag ng araw.
copy.bis: Ang Adlaw moagi ug mas taas ug mas taas nga agianan sa langit sa summer ug mas mubo ug mas ubos sa winter, nga nag-usab sa gitas-on sa kahayag sa adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ultraviolet light from the sun can create thymine dimers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains UV-induced DNA damage (thymine dimers), which is a biology/genetics topic. It provides no information about the different seasons in the Philippines or activities appropriate for each season, so it does not support the competency in any way.

copy.en:
How does sunlight damage DNA?

Ultraviolet light from the sun can create thymine dimers, where two thymine bases stick together and distort the DNA double helix.
copy.tl:
Paano nasisira ng sikat ng araw ang DNA?

Ang ultraviolet light mula sa araw ay maaaring lumikha ng thymine dimers, kung saan magkadikit ang dalawang thymine bases at nababaluktot ang DNA double helix.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagdaot sa kahayag sa adlaw ang DNA?

Ang ultraviolet light gikan sa adlaw makahimo ug thymine dimers, diin magtapot ang duha ka thymine bases ug mabaliko ang DNA double helix.

copy.en: People enjoy eating and relaxing outside on a sunny day, like having a picnic with family and friends.
copy.tl: Masayang kumain at magpahinga sa labas kapag maaraw, tulad ng pagkakaroon ng picnic kasama ang pamilya at mga kaibigan.
copy.bis: Malipayon ang mga tao nga mokaon ug mopahulay sa gawas kon adlaw, sama sa pag-picnic uban sa pamilya ug mga higala.

copy.en: Surface characteristics affect collision outcomes, so a ball bounces higher on hard concrete than on soft carpet.
copy.tl: Ang katangian ng surface ay nakakaapekto sa resulta ng collision, kaya mas mataas tumalbog ang bola sa matigas na semento kaysa sa malambot na carpet.
copy.bis: Ang kinaiya sa surface nakaapekto sa resulta sa collision, busa mas taas molantaw ang bola sa gahi nga semento kaysa sa humok nga carpet.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Weathering occurs when rocks near or on the surface of the Earth are exposed to air, water, and other living things.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about rock weathering, not about using a microscope to observe cell parts. G7-L-2 concerns proper techniques for identifying cell organelles, which has no connection to the card's content.

copy.en: Weathering occurs when rocks near or on the surface of the Earth are exposed to air, water, and other living things.
copy.tl: Ang weathering ay nangyayari kapag ang mga bato malapit o nasa ibabaw ng Earth ay nalantad sa hangin, tubig, at iba pang mga buhay na bagay.
copy.bis: Ang weathering mahitabo kon ang mga bato duol o sa nawong sa Earth maladlad sa hangin, tubig, ug uban pang mga buhing butang.

copy.en: The two types of surface waves are Love waves, which move the ground side-to-side, and Rayleigh waves, which roll along the ground.
copy.tl: Ang dalawang uri ng surface waves ay ang Love waves, na nagpapagalaw sa lupa pakaliwa-kanan, at Rayleigh waves, na gumugulong sa lupa.
copy.bis: Ang duha ka klase sa surface waves mao ang Love waves, nga magpalihok sa yuta paside-side, ug Rayleigh waves, nga moligid sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Swollen lymph nodes in your neck or armpit are a sign your body is fighting off an infection.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the lymphatic/immune response to infection, not the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems. It does not support the competency's required content.

copy.en:
Why do your neck glands swell when you're sick?

Swollen lymph nodes in your neck or armpit are a sign your body is fighting off an infection.
copy.tl:
Bakit namamaga ang kulani kapag may sakit?

Ang namamagang kulani sa leeg o kilikili ay palatandaan na ang katawan ay lumalaban sa impeksiyon.
copy.bis:
Nganong mamaga ang kelenglang kon masakiton?

Ang namaga nga kelenglang sa liog o ilok maoy timaan nga ang lawas nakig-away sa impeksiyon.
